# go-libfossil Documentation (Full)

# Documentation

URL: https://libfossil-docs.daniel-mestas.workers.dev/docs/


go-libfossil reads, writes and syncs Fossil repositories in Go, without cgo. It ships as a Go module and as the `libfossil` command.

- **[Get started](/docs/get-started/)**: install, a first repository from the command line, the library from Go, and a first sync.
- **[Concepts](/docs/concepts/)**: artifacts, the derived tables, the sync protocol, sub-manifests, sparse cones, horizons and signing.
- **[Guides](/docs/guides/)**: production use, migrating from fossil, embedding the CLI, extension points and testing.
- **[Reference](/docs/reference/)**: the Go API, the command line, settings, and conformance with the drafts.
- **[Examples](/docs/examples/)**: runnable programs in the repository.

---

# Get started

URL: https://libfossil-docs.daniel-mestas.workers.dev/docs/get-started/


Install the `libfossil` command, make a first repository from the command line, embed the library in a Go program, and sync with another repository.

- [Install](/docs/get-started/install/): the command, the Go module, and the SQLite driver.
- [Quickstart: the CLI](/docs/get-started/quickstart/): create a repository, commit, and read it back with stock `fossil`.
- [Embed in Go](/docs/get-started/embed-in-go/): create, commit, open and read history from Go.
- [First sync](/docs/get-started/first-sync/): serve a repository, clone it, pull and push.

---

# Install

URL: https://libfossil-docs.daniel-mestas.workers.dev/docs/get-started/install/


go-libfossil is a Go module and a command. Neither needs cgo, a C toolchain or an installed `fossil`.

## The command

```sh
go install github.com/danmestas/go-libfossil/cmd/libfossil@latest
libfossil --help
```

This needs the Go toolchain named in `go.mod` (Go 1.26 or later). The binary is statically linked and runs on Linux, macOS and Windows. Every command is listed in the [CLI reference](/docs/reference/cli/).

## The library

```sh
go get github.com/danmestas/go-libfossil@latest
```

The library talks to SQLite through `database/sql` and does not pick a driver for you. Blank-import exactly one of the two driver modules in your `main` package; importing both panics at start-up.

| Driver | Import | Use it for |
|---|---|---|
| modernc | `_ "github.com/danmestas/go-libfossil/db/driver/modernc"` | servers, command-line tools, desktop: SQLite translated to Go |
| ncruces | `_ "github.com/danmestas/go-libfossil/db/driver/ncruces"` | `GOOS=js` and `GOOS=wasip1` builds: SQLite itself as WebAssembly |

Each driver is its own module, so `go get` it too:

```sh
go get github.com/danmestas/go-libfossil/db/driver/modernc@latest
```

## WebAssembly

With the ncruces driver the module builds for `GOOS=js GOARCH=wasm` (a browser) and `GOOS=wasip1 GOARCH=wasm` (any WASI Preview 1 host). CI builds the module's packages for `js/wasm` on every change. The [wasm example](https://github.com/danmestas/go-libfossil/tree/main/examples/wasm) builds and runs a WASI module.

### TinyGo

The whole public API, the HTTP sync client and signing included, also builds with [TinyGo](https://tinygo.org) for the `wasm` target, which is what makes it small enough to ship with a page or an edge function:

```
tinygo build -target=wasm -no-debug -opt=z -stack-size=1MB -o libfossil.wasm ./examples/tinygo/
wasm-opt -Oz --detect-features --strip-debug --strip-producers libfossil.wasm -o libfossil.wasm
```

- **Size:** for [`examples/tinygo`](https://github.com/danmestas/go-libfossil/tree/main/examples/tinygo), about 1.3 MB gzipped as CI builds it, against about 4.1 MB from the standard toolchain. A program without sync is smaller.
- **Driver:** a TinyGo build imports no SQLite driver. The host registers a `database/sql` driver over its own SQLite; ncruces is for standard Go builds and modernc has no wasm build.
- **Stack:** `-stack-size=1MB`, because TinyGo's default goroutine stack is too small for the deeper paths.
- **Differences:** under TinyGo a sync redirect ends the request with an error instead of being followed, and DNS failures are not classified as transient.

CI builds `examples/tinygo` with TinyGo 0.43 on every change.

## Next

- [Quickstart: the CLI](/docs/get-started/quickstart/)
- [Embed in Go](/docs/get-started/embed-in-go/)

# Quickstart: the CLI

URL: https://libfossil-docs.daniel-mestas.workers.dev/docs/get-started/quickstart/


Create a repository, commit a file, and read the result with stock `fossil`. The `libfossil` command drives the same code as the library, and the file it writes is an ordinary Fossil repository.

## Create a repository and a checkout

```sh
libfossil repo new notes.fossil
mkdir work && cd work
libfossil -R ../notes.fossil repo open .
```

```text
created repository: notes.fossil
opened checkout in . (repo: /home/ana/notes.fossil)
empty repository -- no checkins yet
```

`repo open` writes a `.fslckout` file in the directory. Commands run inside the checkout find the repository through it, so `-R` is only needed to open it.

## Commit

```sh
echo '# notes' > README.md
libfossil repo add README.md
libfossil repo ci -m "first notes" --user ana
```

```text
ADDED    README.md
checkin 542a963405 (rid=2)
```

The check-in name is the hash of the manifest, which includes the time, so yours differs. `--user` sets the name on the check-in; without it the OS user name is used.

## Read the history

```sh
libfossil repo timeline
```

```text
542a963405  2026-10-23 21:00  ana  first notes
```

The repository is a Fossil repository, so the `fossil` binary reads it unchanged:

```sh
fossil timeline -R ../notes.fossil
```

```text
=== 2026-10-23 ===
21:00:14 [542a963405] first notes (user: ana tags: trunk)
+++ no more data (1) +++
```

## Next

- [Embed in Go](/docs/get-started/embed-in-go/): the same steps from a Go program.
- [First sync](/docs/get-started/first-sync/): serve the repository and clone it.
- [CLI reference](/docs/reference/cli/): every command and flag.
- [Migrating from fossil](/docs/guides/migrating-from-fossil/): how the commands map to fossil's.

# Embed in Go

URL: https://libfossil-docs.daniel-mestas.workers.dev/docs/get-started/embed-in-go/


The `libfossil` package does what the command does, as typed Go values instead of command output. This program creates a repository, commits a file and reads the history back.

## Set up

```sh
mkdir notes && cd notes
go mod init example.com/notes
go get github.com/danmestas/go-libfossil@latest github.com/danmestas/go-libfossil/db/driver/modernc@latest
```

The blank import of `db/driver/modernc` registers the SQLite driver. A program registers exactly one; see [Install](/docs/get-started/install/) for the choice.

## Create, commit, read

```go
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"log"

	"github.com/danmestas/go-libfossil"
	_ "github.com/danmestas/go-libfossil/db/driver/modernc"
)

func main() {
	r, err := libfossil.Create("notes.fossil", libfossil.CreateOpts{User: "ana"})
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
	defer r.Close()

	rid, uuid, err := r.Commit(libfossil.CommitOpts{
		Files:   []libfossil.FileToCommit{{Name: "README.md", Content: []byte("# notes\n")}},
		Comment: "first notes",
		User:    "ana",
	})
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
	fmt.Println("committed", uuid[:10], "rid", rid)

	entries, err := r.Timeline(libfossil.TimelineOpts{Limit: 10})
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
	for _, e := range entries {
		fmt.Println(e.UUID[:10], e.User, e.Comment)
	}

	files, err := r.ListFiles(rid)
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
	for _, f := range files {
		fmt.Println(f.Name)
	}
}
```

```sh
go run .
```

```text
committed ee68ff62c5 rid 2
ee68ff62c5 ana first notes
README.md
```

`Commit` returns the check-in's row id in the `blob` table and its full name. `CommitOpts.Files` lists file contents directly; no checkout or working directory is involved. To commit on top of an existing check-in, set `ParentID`: the files you pass replace the parent's entries of the same name and the rest of the parent's tree is carried forward, as `fossil commit` does.

The file is an ordinary Fossil repository: `fossil timeline -R notes.fossil` shows the same check-in.

## Open an existing repository

```go
r, err := libfossil.Open("notes.fossil")
if err != nil {
	log.Fatal(err)
}
defer r.Close()

tip, err := r.BranchTip("trunk")
if err != nil {
	log.Fatal(err)
}
files, err := r.ListFiles(tip)
```

`Open` fails if the file does not exist; `Create` fails if it does. Reads through one `*Repo` may run concurrently; writes serialize in SQLite. Close the handle once, when you are done with it. [Production patterns](/docs/guides/production/) covers error handling, contexts and handle lifetime.

# First sync

URL: https://libfossil-docs.daniel-mestas.workers.dev/docs/get-started/first-sync/


Two repositories exchange check-ins with Fossil's sync protocol over HTTP. `libfossil repo serve` is a sync server; `Clone`, `Repo.Sync` and `Repo.Pull` are the client. Either side can be stock `fossil`. [Sync](/docs/concepts/sync/) explains the protocol.

## Serve a repository

```sh
libfossil -R notes.fossil repo serve
```

```text
serving /home/ana/notes.fossil on http://127.0.0.1:8080 (Ctrl-C to stop)
```

`--addr` changes the bind address. The server answers sync requests only; it has no web interface.

An unauthenticated client gets the capabilities of the `nobody` user, which a new repository sets as `fossil new` does: clone and read, no check-in. To let a client push, give a user the check-in capability `i` and a password:

```sh
libfossil -R notes.fossil repo user add --cap=i bo
libfossil -R notes.fossil repo user passwd bo
```

Both commands print the user's generated password.

## Clone

From the command line, with either tool:

```sh
libfossil repo clone http://127.0.0.1:8080 copy.fossil
fossil clone http://127.0.0.1:8080 copy2.fossil
```

```text
Cloned into copy.fossil
  Rounds:       2
  Blobs:        2
  Project-code: ec1581be7066e95dd3b9ee14b91ab3f258221ce4
```

`repo clone` also clones part of a repository: `--cone` by path and `--horizon` by age. See [Sparse cones](/docs/concepts/sparse-cones/) and [Horizons](/docs/concepts/horizons/).

## Clone, commit, push and pull from Go

```go
package main

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"log"
	"os"

	"github.com/danmestas/go-libfossil"
	_ "github.com/danmestas/go-libfossil/db/driver/modernc"
)

func main() {
	ctx := context.Background()
	url := "http://127.0.0.1:8080"

	r, res, err := libfossil.Clone(ctx, "copy.fossil", libfossil.NewHTTPTransport(url), libfossil.CloneOpts{})
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
	defer r.Close()
	fmt.Println("cloned", res.BlobsRecvd, "blobs in", res.Rounds, "rounds")

	tip, err := r.BranchTip("trunk")
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
	if _, _, err := r.Commit(libfossil.CommitOpts{
		Files:    []libfossil.FileToCommit{{Name: "TODO.md", Content: []byte("- ship\n")}},
		Comment:  "add a todo",
		User:     "bo",
		ParentID: tip,
	}); err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}

	pushed, err := r.Sync(ctx, libfossil.NewHTTPTransport(url), libfossil.SyncOpts{
		Push: true, Pull: true, User: "bo", Password: os.Getenv("NOTES_PASSWORD"),
	})
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
	fmt.Println("sent", pushed.FilesSent, "received", pushed.FilesRecvd)

	pulled, err := r.Pull(ctx, url, libfossil.PullOpts{})
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
	fmt.Println("pull rounds", pulled.Rounds)
}
```

```sh
NOTES_PASSWORD=... go run .
```

```text
cloned 2 blobs in 2 rounds
sent 2 received 0
pull rounds 1
```

`Clone` creates the file and fails if it exists. `Sync` with `Push` and `Pull` runs one session in both directions until neither side has anything the other lacks; `Pull` is a pull-only shorthand that takes a URL. Without `User`, a session runs as `nobody`. Pass a context with a deadline in a service: a stalled peer otherwise holds the call open.

The commit made in the clone went to the origin:

```sh
libfossil -R notes.fossil repo timeline
```

```text
fb5af4c078  2026-10-23 21:02  bo  add a todo
ee68ff62c5  2026-10-23 21:02  ana  first notes
```

## Next

- [Sync](/docs/concepts/sync/): the cards and rounds behind these calls.
- [Production patterns](/docs/guides/production/): contexts, errors and telemetry for a long-running service.

# Concepts

URL: https://libfossil-docs.daniel-mestas.workers.dev/docs/concepts/


How a Fossil repository is put together, and how go-libfossil implements it. Each page names the Internet-Draft in [`conformance/rfcs/`](https://github.com/danmestas/go-libfossil/tree/main/conformance/rfcs) that specifies the behaviour.

- [Architecture](/docs/concepts/architecture/): packages, drivers, observers and the simulator.
- [Artifacts](/docs/concepts/artifacts/): the text manifests that make up history, and how they are named.
- [Repository state](/docs/concepts/repository-state/): the tables derived from the artifacts.
- [Sync](/docs/concepts/sync/): the card protocol that clones, pulls and pushes.
- [Sub-manifests](/docs/concepts/sub-manifests/): check-ins written as trees instead of flat file lists.
- [Sparse cones](/docs/concepts/sparse-cones/): holding part of a repository by path.
- [Horizons](/docs/concepts/horizons/): holding part of a repository by age.
- [Signing](/docs/concepts/signing/): clear-signed check-ins and signed horizon seeds.
