## Overview

libfossil is a pure-Go library and CLI that reads and writes Fossil SCM's
`.fossil` SQLite repositories. The public surface (package `libfossil`)
exposes `Repo`, `Create`, `Open`, `Clone`, checkout, and check-in
operations; internals live under `internal/`. SQLite access is mediated
by a pluggable driver layer in `db/`, with two shippable drivers
(`modernc`, `ncruces`) selected by blank import. Instrumentation is
pulled in by implementing the `SyncObserver` / `CheckoutObserver`
interfaces; an optional OTel adapter lives in its own submodule. A
deterministic simulator under `dst/` plus a `BUGGIFY` fault-injection
harness in `simio/` exercise concurrent repo operations under a seed.

## Module layout

The library is a Go workspace (`go.work`) of four modules: the root, the
two driver modules, and the OTel observer. (The documentation site under
`docs/site` has its own `go.mod` and is not in the workspace.) Layout:

- **Root package `libfossil`** — thin facade over `internal/repo`,
  `internal/sync`, and `internal/checkout`. Main files: `fossil.go`
  (Create, Open, Clone), `repo.go` (Repo handle + DB accessor),
  `checkout.go`, `checkout_sparse.go` (cones and horizons),
  `repo_checkout.go`, `repo_merge.go`, `repo_sync.go`, `repo_pull.go`,
  `repo_sparse.go`, `repo_submanifest.go`, `repo_history.go`,
  `repo_admin.go`, `repo_extras.go`, `required_content*.go`,
  `horizon_*.go`, `signing.go`, `transport.go`, `observer.go`, `types.go`,
  `errors.go`, `julian.go`.
- **`cli/`** — Kong command definitions. `repo.go` aggregates 43
  subcommands (`new`, `clone`, `ci`, `co`, `timeline`, `diff`, `merge`,
  `tag`, `branch`, `uv`, `stash`, `bisect`, `annotate`, `user`, `serve`,
  `cone`, `submanifests`, etc.). Intended to be embedded by any `main` that
  wants a fossil-shaped CLI.
- **`cmd/libfossil/`** — the shipped binary. `main.go` wires Kong and
  dispatches to `cli`; `driver_modernc.go` and `driver_ncruces.go` select
  the driver by build tag (`modernc` by default, `ncruces` under
  `test_ncruces`).
- **`internal/`** — private implementation, grouped by concern:
  - Storage layer: `blob`, `content`, `manifest`, `deck`, `delta`,
    `hash`, `fsltype`, `repo` (schema + DB boot), `tag`, `leaf`,
    `clearsign`.
  - Sparse and horizon stores: `cone`, `horizon` (held set and seed).
  - Working-tree operations: `checkout` (checkin, extract, update,
    revert, fork, rename, status), `vfile`, `merge` (three-way, ancestor,
    detect, resolve, strategies), `diff`, `annotate`, `undo`, `stash`,
    `bisect`, `branch`, `path`.
  - Sync / transport: `sync` (client, handler, clone, session,
    ckin-lock, serve-http, table-sync, UV, sparse and horizon serving),
    `xfer` (card codec).
  - Housekeeping: `auth`, `shun`, `verify`, `search`, `uv`, `testdriver`.
- **`db/`** — SQLite abstraction (see below).
- **`db/driver/modernc`**, **`db/driver/ncruces`** — separate modules,
  each registers exactly one `database/sql` driver.
- **`observer/otel/`** — separate module implementing the observer
  interfaces against OpenTelemetry.
- **`dst/`** — deterministic simulator (`simulator.go`, `node.go`,
  `network.go`, `peer_network.go`, `mock_fossil.go`, `invariants.go`,
  `event.go`) with scenario-style tests.
- **`simio/`** — deterministic IO primitives: `SimClock`, seeded
  `Rand`, in-memory storage, and the global `Buggify` switch.
- **`testutil/`** — shared test helpers for the rest of the tree.

## Storage model

A `.fossil` file is a SQLite database. All repository state — blobs,
manifests, tags, branches, unversioned files, tickets, wiki, config,
users — lives in that file. libfossil does not maintain any sidecar
state for the repo itself (a working tree has its own SQLite DB).

Content is stored **content-addressed** in the `blob` table, keyed by
either SHA1 or SHA3-256 names (the repository's hash policy picks which
names new content; see [Artifacts](/docs/concepts/artifacts/)). Every blob is
zlib-compressed with a 4-byte big-endian uncompressed-size prefix;
`internal/blob.Compress` and `Decompress` handle that framing. Blobs may
be stored as full content or as deltas against a parent; reconstruction
walks the chain and applies deltas via `internal/content.Expand`, with
cycle detection. `internal/content.Verify` rehashes expanded content
against the stored UUID.

**Structural artifacts** are themselves blobs whose text describes a
check-in (a manifest), a tag change, a wiki edit, a ticket change, an
attachment, a technote, a forum post, or a cluster. `internal/deck`
parses and marshals them and `internal/manifest` builds check-ins;
"crosslinking" (`internal/manifest/crosslink.go`) is the step that
projects an artifact's effects into derived tables (`mlink`, `plink`,
`event`, `tagxref`, etc.) so queries like timeline and checkout work
without re-parsing blobs. See [Repository state](/docs/concepts/repository-state/).

## Driver layer

`db/` is a thin wrapper over `database/sql`. See
[`db/doc.go`](https://github.com/danmestas/go-libfossil/blob/main/db/doc.go). A driver registers at `init` time via
`db.Register(DriverConfig{Name, BuildDSN})`; exactly one registration is
allowed (a second call panics). Library embedders blank-import exactly one
driver. `db.Open` / `db.OpenWith` look up the registered driver, run
`BuildDSN(path, pragmas)` to produce the DSN, and then call `sql.Open` with
that driver name. Both shipped drivers construct
`file:<path>?_pragma=k(v)&...` DSNs — differing only in the `database/sql`
driver name they register under (`"sqlite"` for modernc, `"sqlite3"` for
ncruces).

Shipped drivers:

- **`db/driver/modernc`** — default for `cmd/libfossil`. Blank-imports
  `modernc.org/sqlite`, a pure-Go, CGo-free translation of SQLite with full
  filesystem access.
- **`db/driver/ncruces`** — blank-imports `github.com/ncruces/go-sqlite3`,
  which runs SQLite as WebAssembly. Has a `ncruces_js.go` variant for
  `GOOS=js` / browser targets. Used for `GOOS=wasip1` builds and by
  `go build -tags test_ncruces ./cmd/libfossil`.

## Sync protocol

`internal/sync` implements Fossil's sync-over-HTTP protocol as a client
and a stateless server, with the card codec in `internal/xfer`. See
[Sync](/docs/concepts/sync/) for the protocol and where each part lives.

## Observer model

The core keeps instrumentation as a non-goal; hooks are plain Go
interfaces on the public API. `SyncObserver` and `CheckoutObserver` in
[`observer.go`](https://github.com/danmestas/go-libfossil/blob/main/observer.go) define lifecycle events (session
start/end, per-round stats, extract/scan/commit phases). `NopSyncObserver`
/ `NopCheckoutObserver` are zero-cost defaults; `StdoutSyncObserver` /
`StdoutCheckoutObserver` log to stderr for quick debugging.

For OpenTelemetry, [`observer/otel`](https://github.com/danmestas/go-libfossil/tree/main/observer/otel/) is a separate Go
module so the core doesn't pull in the OTel SDK. Users import it
explicitly when they want traces, metrics, or structured logs.

See [Extension Points](/docs/guides/extension-points/) for the full observer
contract and a worked example of a custom observer.

## DST / simulation

`dst/` runs many Fossil nodes deterministically under a seed. A
`Simulator` (`dst/simulator.go`) owns a priority-queue event loop, a
`SimNetwork`, a `simio.SimClock`, and a set of `Node` actors. Scenarios
schedule clones, check-ins, merges, UV pushes, and partitions, and
tests assert invariants (`dst/invariants.go`, `crosslink_completeness_test.go`).

Fault injection has two forms. `simio.Buggify(p)` is a global
probability gate that returns `false` in production but flips `true`
with probability `p` once the simulator enables it; the blob and content
layers use it. The sync code instead asks a `BuggifyChecker` passed in
its options, at named sites such as `clone.emitCloneBatch.truncate` and
`handler.handleGimme.skip`; a nil checker injects nothing. `SeededBuggify`
in `dst` implements `BuggifyChecker` from a seeded random source.

See [Testing](/docs/guides/testing/) for running the DST matrix, seed sweeps,
and the driver test matrix.

---

# Artifacts

URL: https://libfossil-docs.daniel-mestas.workers.dev/docs/concepts/artifacts/


Everything a Fossil repository records is an **artifact**: a run of bytes, named by its own hash, that is never changed once written. File contents are artifacts. So are check-ins, tags, wiki pages and tickets, which are written as text **cards**. The format is `draft-fossil-artifact-format-00`.

## Names

An artifact's name is the hash of its exact stored bytes, with nothing added or stripped (§3.1). A 40-digit name is SHA-1; a 64-digit name is SHA3-256. The length alone tells which (§3.2). A signed artifact's name covers its signature wrapper too, so signing a check-in changes its name.

The repository's **hash policy** decides which algorithm names new content (§7.1):

| Policy | Names new content with |
|---|---|
| `sha1`, `auto` | SHA-1 |
| `sha3`, `sha3-only`, `shun-sha1` | SHA3-256 |

A repository with no policy set uses `sha3` unless it holds SHA-1 names and no SHA3 ones, in which case it uses `auto` (§7.2). A new repository is `sha3`. Names already assigned never change (§7.6). `Repo.SetHashPolicy(name)` sets the policy as `fossil hash-policy` does.

## Structural artifacts and cards

A structural artifact is lines of cards: a capital letter, then space-separated arguments, with the cards in sorted order and a `Z` card last (§4). There are eight types, and each allows a fixed set of cards (§5.1, §5.2):

| Type | External name | Allowed cards |
|---|---|---|
| MANIFEST | `checkin` | B C D F N P Q R T U Z |
| CLUSTER | `cluster` | M Z |
| CONTROL | `tag` | D T U Z |
| WIKI | `wiki` | C D L N P U W Z |
| TICKET | `ticket` | D J K U Z |
| ATTACHMENT | `attachment` | A C D N U Z |
| EVENT | `technote` | C D E N P T U W Z |
| FORUM | `forumpost` | D G H I N P U W Z |

Any other byte string is plain content, such as a file's bytes. A parser rejects a structural artifact with a card its type does not allow, or without one its type requires.

[Sub-manifests](/docs/concepts/sub-manifests/) add an `S` card and a ninth type.

## A check-in manifest

This is a check-in made with `libfossil repo ci`:

```
C unsigned
D 2026-10-23T20:45:21.324
F docs/x.md a09fd4d0069e85b78c5234233ffb67179d30e19c2ec94629d224257a920c1234
F src/a.c 7eae391285a140af77b34475a35c4790095acb1f0f5e6ec7e10e962b2405de07
F src/vendor/v.c bedef797cd3184c3c7e620c5c231bbdd523f52ab19ca6301d037c7f2a3f99780
P 2afc4615dadbd7743716f8037223578d7d07a79ebc2cbfd5ba1b6028f133c7f2
R 43fe2394e6714e382e2f6563c13cf020
U dmestas
Z 56b668a3573378eb3e2387902909b385
```

- `C`: the check-in comment.
- `D`: the date, UTC.
- `F`: one per file: path and content hash, then optional permissions and an old name for a rename.
- `P`: the parent check-ins. The first is the primary parent; the rest are merge parents.
- `R`: an MD5 over every file's name, size and content (§6.3). A commit reads its manifest back and checks it. Over a sparse store there is no `R` card.
- `U`: the user.
- `Z`: the MD5 of every byte before it (§6.2).

The first check-in on a branch also carries `T` cards, such as `T *branch * trunk` and `T *sym-trunk *`. A **delta manifest** carries a `B` card naming a baseline manifest, and its `F` cards record only the differences from it (§8).

The name of this check-in is the SHA3-256 of exactly these bytes: `libfossil repo hash --sha3` over the output of `repo cat` prints `7507cc8c3e...`, the name the timeline shows.

## Deltas

Content is stored in the `blob` table, zlib-compressed behind a 4-byte size prefix. A blob can also be stored as a **delta** against another blob, with the pair recorded in the `delta` table (`rid`, `srcid`). Reading it applies the chain of deltas back to a full blob, and the result must hash to the blob's name.

A delta is a header with the target length, a run of copy and insert segments, and a trailer with a checksum of the result (`draft-fossil-delta-format-00` §3). Integers are written in base 64. A delta does not name its source; the storage layer records that (§1).

As in fossil, deltas run backwards: a new version is stored whole and its predecessor is rewritten as a delta against it, so the newest version of a file is always one read away.

## Where the code is

- `internal/deck`: parse and marshal cards, the `Z` card, signature-wrapper stripping.
- `internal/manifest`: build check-ins, compute the `R` card, crosslink.
- `internal/delta`: create and apply deltas (`Create`, `Apply`).
- `internal/hash`: SHA-1 and SHA3-256 names and the hash policy.
- `internal/blob` and `internal/content`: compressed storage, delta chains, verification.

---

# Repository state

URL: https://libfossil-docs.daniel-mestas.workers.dev/docs/concepts/repository-state/


[Artifacts](/docs/concepts/artifacts/) are the only facts a repository records. Everything else, such as which check-in is the tip of trunk, which branch a check-in is on, or which leaves are open, follows from them. `draft-fossil-repo-state-00` specifies that derivation, so two implementations reading the same artifacts reach the same answers. The one exception is the current trunk, which also reads the repository's `main-branch` setting (§9).

## The tables

A `.fossil` file stores the artifacts in `blob` and `delta`, and keeps the derived state in tables beside them, so a query does not re-parse every artifact.

| Table | Holds |
|---|---|
| `blob` | Every artifact, compressed, by `rid` and name (`uuid`). A row with no content is a phantom. |
| `delta` | Which blobs are stored as deltas, and against what. |
| `phantom` | Names the repository knows of but does not hold yet. |
| `event` | One row per check-in, tag, wiki edit, ticket change and so on: the timeline. |
| `plink` | Parent links between check-ins, with which parent is primary (§3). |
| `mlink` | Which file changed in which check-in, and from which earlier version. |
| `filename` | The file names `mlink` refers to. |
| `tag`, `tagxref` | Tag names, and each tag's effect on each check-in: cancel, singleton or propagating (§5). |
| `leaf` | Check-ins with no child on their own branch (§7). |
| `orphan` | Delta manifests whose baseline is absent. |

`blob` and `delta` are the source. The others are derived.

## Crosslinking

**Crosslinking** reads one artifact and writes its effects into the derived tables (§4). A check-in adds its `plink` and `mlink` rows and its `event` row. Its `T` cards, or a control artifact's, set `tagxref` rows and propagate along primary children until a cancel or another value blocks them (§5.4). Leaves are rechecked as parents gain children and as tags move (§7.6).

Artifacts can arrive in any order. Sync, clone, a commit and a rebuild all crosslink, and an artifact whose parent has not arrived yet is linked again when it does.

Branches are not stored as such. A check-in's branch is the value of its `branch` tag, inherited from its primary parent unless a tag on it says otherwise (§6). Name resolution (§8) turns a branch name, tag or `trunk` into one check-in: `Repo.ResolveVersion(name)`. `Repo.CurrentTrunk()` returns the tip of the main branch (§9).

## Rebuild gives the same rows

Because the derived tables are a function of the artifacts, they can be thrown away and computed again. go-libfossil's rebuild (`verify.Rebuild`, internal) empties the crosslinked tables and runs the same crosslink sweep a clone runs, so derived state has one owner. The tables it refills are `event`, `plink`, `leaf`, `mlink`, `tagxref`, `forumpost`, `attachment`, `backlink`, `cherrypick` and `orphan`, plus the sync bookkeeping tables `unclustered` and `unsent`.

The conformance suite checks this against fossil itself:

- Each scripted case in `conformance/repostate_*_test.go` loads a sequence of artifacts into go-libfossil (one sweep, one artifact at a time, and through rebuild) and into fossil(1). The rows must equal the expectation written from the draft, and fossil's rows must equal it too: its per-artifact crosslink for a crosslink case, `fossil rebuild` on a copy for a rebuild case. The compared tables are `plink`, `tagxref`, `event`, `phantom`, `leaf`, `orphan` and `mlink`.
- `TestRepoStateCorpus` takes real repositories (named in `CONFORMANCE_REPOS`) and derives their tables three ways: `fossil rebuild` on one copy, as the reference; go-libfossil's rebuild on a second; a crosslink sweep over emptied tables on a third. It compares `event`, `leaf`, `mlink`, `phantom`, `plink` and `tagxref` column by column. It runs only when fossil(1) is present.

Where fossil departs from the draft text, the case records it and names the draft change proposed. The requirements are listed in `conformance/requirements/repostate.tsv`.

## Where the code is

- `internal/manifest`: crosslinking (`crosslink.go`), re-derivation (`rederive.go`), the timeline.
- `internal/tag`: tag application and propagation.
- `internal/leaf`: the leaf table.
- `internal/verify`: integrity checks and rebuild.
- `internal/repo`: the schema and the `main-branch` setting.

---

# Sync

URL: https://libfossil-docs.daniel-mestas.workers.dev/docs/concepts/sync/


Two repositories exchange artifacts with Fossil's sync protocol: text cards carried in HTTP POST bodies, one request and one reply per round. go-libfossil implements both ends, and talks to stock fossil, zit and other go-libfossil peers. The governing text is `draft-fossil-sync-protocol-00`.

## Messages and cards

A message is a list of cards, one per line: a card name, then space-separated arguments, and for content cards a byte payload after the line (§5). Unknown pragmas are ignored, so a peer can add new ones without breaking old ones (§3.5).

The client POSTs each request to the repository URL (§4). The body is a 4-byte big-endian length followed by a zlib stream (§4.1). A clone reply may be sent uncompressed, because its `cfile` payloads are already compressed.

The cards that move artifacts:

| Card | Meaning | Draft |
|---|---|---|
| `igot HASH` | I hold this artifact. `igot HASH 1` marks it private. | §8.6 |
| `gimme HASH` | Send me this artifact. | §8.6 |
| `file HASH SIZE` | The artifact's bytes, or a delta against another artifact (`file HASH DELTASRC SIZE`). Used by push and pull. | §7.1 |
| `cfile HASH USIZE CSIZE` | The artifact as the sender stores it, compressed, sent verbatim. Used by clone. | §7.2 |
| `push` / `pull` | The operation, with the server and project codes. | §3.2 |
| `clone 3 SEQNO` / `clone_seqno N` | The clone loop's position. | §8.2 |
| `login USER NONCE SIGNATURE` | Authentication. | §6.1 |
| `pragma NAME ...` | Version negotiation and extensions. | §9 |
| `error` / `message` | Errors and notices. | §10 |

Unversioned files travel as `uvigot`, `uvgimme` and `uvfile` (§7.3, §8.5.1). Configuration travels as `reqconfig` and `config` (§9.3).

## Rounds

A session is a loop of rounds. Each round the client says what it holds (`igot`) and what it wants (`gimme`), and sends the content the server asked for in the last reply. The server answers in kind. A `gimme` is never sent for a shunned artifact or one the peer has said it lacks (§8.8).

The client decides when to stop. It issues another round only while the last round made progress: it stored content and still has phantoms (artifacts it knows by name but does not hold), it queued content to send, or one of the unversioned-file or clone conditions holds (§3.7). Phantoms alone do not keep the loop running. The server sends no completion card.

## Clone, pull, push

- **Clone** starts with `clone 3 1`. The server sends its stored blobs as `cfile` cards in batches and a `clone_seqno` saying where to continue; zero ends the transfer and one cleanup round follows (§8.1 to §8.4). Artifacts the rounds leave missing stay phantoms, as with fossil's clone, unless `CloneOpts.PullPhantoms` is set.
- **Pull** sends `pull` each round and receives what it lacks.
- **Push** sends `push` each round and answers the server's `gimme` cards with `file` cards.
- **Sync** sends both.

After artifacts arrive they are [crosslinked](/docs/concepts/repository-state/), so branches, tags and leaves follow from the artifacts each side holds, not from anything sent on the wire (§8.6.1).

## Login

A named user signs each request (§6). `NONCE` is the SHA-1 of the request body after the login line. The shared secret is `SHA1(project-code "/" login "/" password)`, and `SIGNATURE` is `SHA1(NONCE || shared-secret)`. The first clone round carries no login. A request with no login runs as `nobody`. Once the server announces a version that reads it, the login moves to the `x-f-l-c` cookie (§6.5).

The server checks the user's capabilities from its `user` table (§6.6). In a new repository `nobody` may clone and pull but not push; grant more with `Repo.SetCaps`.

## The server is stateless

Each request is handled on its own (§8.9). The server keeps no session between rounds, so any number of clients can sync against one repository, and a server can sit behind any HTTP stack.

```go
repo, err := libfossil.Open("repo.fossil")
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}
defer repo.Close()

mux := http.NewServeMux()
mux.HandleFunc("/", repo.XferHandler())
mux.HandleFunc("/healthz", func(w http.ResponseWriter, _ *http.Request) {})
log.Fatal(http.ListenAndServe(":8080", mux))
```

- `Repo.XferHandler()` returns an `http.HandlerFunc` that decodes a request, handles it and encodes the reply. A non-POST request gets a plain page.
- `Repo.ServeHTTP(ctx, addr)` runs a server on `addr` until `ctx` is cancelled. `libfossil repo serve --addr 127.0.0.1:8080` does the same from the command line.
- `Repo.HandleSync(ctx, payload)` and `HandleSyncWithOpts` take and return raw message bytes, for an embedder with its own transport. Over HTTP, pass the `x-f-l-c` cookie in `HandleOpts.LoginCookie` and the client address in `HandleOpts.RemoteAddr`; `XferHandler` and `ServeHTTP` fill both themselves.

## The client

```go
t := libfossil.NewHTTPTransport("https://example.com/repo")

repo, res, err := libfossil.Clone(ctx, "repo.fossil", t, libfossil.CloneOpts{
    User: "alice", Password: "secret",
})

sr, err := repo.Sync(ctx, t, libfossil.SyncOpts{
    Push: true, Pull: true, User: "alice", Password: "secret",
})
```

`Transport` is one method, `RoundTrip(ctx, payload) ([]byte, error)`, so any byte pipe works. `NewHTTPTransport` takes `WithHTTPClient` for a custom `http.Client`. `Repo.Pull(ctx, url, PullOpts{})` is a pull-only shortcut over HTTP.

`SyncOpts` also turns on unversioned files (`UV`), private artifacts (`Private`, §7.5), fossil's `--share-links` (`ShareLinks`, §9.5) and go-libfossil's own table sync (`XTableSync`). `SyncResult` reports rounds, files and bytes each way, and errors.

The `libfossil` binary clones (`repo clone`) and serves (`repo serve`). Pull, push and sync are library calls.

## Check-in lock

A client that is about to commit can ask the server to hold the parent with `pragma ci-lock` (§9.4). The server records a `ci-lock-<parent hash>` row in its `config` table and reports a conflicting holder with `ci-lock-fail`. A lock goes stale after the repository's `lock-timeout` setting, 60 seconds when unset (`DefaultCkinLockTimeout`). Fossil uses the same row, so a repository served by both shares one lock table.

## Shunned artifacts

A shunned artifact is never requested, and one that arrives is dropped rather than stored. The shun list itself can travel as the `shun` configuration group (§9.3).

## Extensions

Pragmas carry the extensions. Each is ignored by a peer that does not know it.

- [Sparse cones](/docs/concepts/sparse-cones/): `pragma cone`, answered by `cone-served` (`draft-fossil-sparse-cone-00` §6).
- [Horizons](/docs/concepts/horizons/): `horizon-served`, the seed and the cursor (`draft-fossil-horizon-00` §6).
- [Sub-manifests](/docs/concepts/sub-manifests/): `send-submanifests` and `avoid-submanifests` (`draft-fossil-submanifests-00` §7.2).

## Where the code is

- **Client** (`internal/sync/client.go`, `clone.go`, `session.go`): drives the rounds. Supports clone, pull, push and sync, plus unversioned files and config table sync (`client_tablesync.go`).
- **Server** (`internal/sync/handler.go`, `serve_http.go`, `handler_uv.go`, `handler_tablesync.go`): one request in, one reply out.
- **Cards** (`internal/xfer`): encoding and decoding of messages and cards.
- **Check-in lock** (`internal/sync/ckin_lock.go`).
- **Table sync deletes** (`internal/sync/xdelete.go`): an `xdelete` card removes a synced table row, or leaves a tombstone where the row is absent.
- **Public entry points**: `Clone` in `fossil.go`; `Repo.Sync`, `HandleSync`, `XferHandler` and `ServeHTTP` in `repo_sync.go`; `Repo.Pull` in `repo_pull.go`; `NewHTTPTransport` in `transport.go`.

---

# Sub-manifests

URL: https://libfossil-docs.daniel-mestas.workers.dev/docs/concepts/sub-manifests/


A check-in manifest has one `F` card per file in the tree, not per changed file. Its size grows with the width of the tree, and every check-in pays it. Sub-manifests split the file list into a tree of smaller artifacts, so a typical check-in rewrites the root manifest and one leaf. The format is `draft-fossil-submanifests-00`.

Two implementations exist: zit writes, reads and serves sub-manifests, and go-libfossil writes and reads them. The two interoperate. Fossil does not implement the draft (§1.3).

## The tree

A **sub-manifest** carries a contiguous slice of a check-in's sorted file list: `F` cards in a leaf, or `S` cards that point to lower sub-manifests in an interior node. A manifest whose files are given by `S` cards is a **tree manifest**. Walking the tree in order gives exactly the file list a flat manifest would carry (§5.1).

```
S src/a.c 5d0c...
```

An `S` card names the first file of the slice and the sub-manifest that holds it (§3.6). Sub-manifests are a ninth artifact type, `submanifest` (§4.1).

Where the boundaries fall depends only on file names. A name starts a new leaf when the SHA3-256 of the name has at least `k` leading zero bits (§6.1). Editing a file changes one leaf. Adding or removing a name can change a few until the boundaries line up again (§6.5). `k` is never written into an artifact, and readers do not need it.

## Settings

Three repository settings control writing. They travel by configuration exchange: a clone asks for them in its cleanup round and adopts them, and a pull does not (§6.3).

| Setting | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `enable-submanifests` | Write new check-ins as trees (§8.1). | off |
| `submanifest-k` | The partition parameter, 1 to 12 (§6.3). | unpinned |
| `submanifest-auto-retune` | Let a commit re-pin `k` when it drifts (§6.4). | off |

When emission is first enabled with no pinned `k`, one is selected by the cost in §6.3 over the file list of the main branch's tip (the newest check-in when no check-in is on the main branch), then refined by replaying the last 200 check-ins. A tree with too few files for any `k` to split has no selection, and enabling fails; give `--k` explicitly. A pinned `k` outside 1 to 12 makes commits fall back to flat manifests with a warning.

A re-tune is forward only. The next commit shares only the sub-manifests whose bytes are the same under both values. With `submanifest-auto-retune` on, a commit re-pins `k` when the best candidate costs more than 15% less than the pinned one, zit's margin. With it off, the drift is only logged.

## Command line

```
$ libfossil -R repo.fossil repo submanifests status
enable-submanifests:     off
submanifest-k:           (unpinned)
submanifest-auto-retune: off
trees in repository:     no

$ libfossil -R repo.fossil repo submanifests enable --k 4
$ libfossil -R repo.fossil repo submanifests retune --k 5
$ libfossil -R repo.fossil repo submanifests disable
```

- `enable [--k N]`: write new check-ins as trees, pinning `k` (selected when `--k` is absent). It prints a warning that fossil peers will be refused the trees.
- `retune --k N`: re-pin `k` for later commits.
- `disable`: write flat manifests again. Existing trees stay.
- `status`: show the three settings and whether the repository holds any tree.

The library calls are `Repo.EnableSubmanifests(k)` (0 selects; it returns the pinned `k` and the warning), `Repo.RetuneSubmanifests(k)` and `Repo.DisableSubmanifests()`.

## Sync

A peer that reads sub-manifests says so with `pragma send-submanifests` in every request and reply (§7.2). go-libfossil always sends it, whatever its settings. A peer that has not sent it is refused every sub-manifest and every tree manifest, with an explicit error. Nothing is converted or downgraded. Every fossil release is such a peer, so a repository with trees serves fossil only the history before the first tree.

A server whose `enable-submanifests` is off also sends `pragma avoid-submanifests`. It binds only commits made during that sync session. go-libfossil commits outside a session and pushes afterwards, so the pragma never binds its commits: whether a commit writes a tree is decided by the local `enable-submanifests` alone. The pragma does not stop a server storing a tree pushed to it.

## Things to know before enabling

- **It is a flag day.** Every reader of the repository must understand sub-manifests before any writer emits one (§8). A repository that a fossil peer serves must not enable them.
- **Trees cannot be retired.** Disabling stops new trees; artifact names are immutable, so the ones written stay, and fossil peers are still refused them.
- **Sparse stores hold every tree node.** A [sparse store](/docs/concepts/sparse-cones/) keeps all sub-manifest nodes, so history stays readable without the file content.

## Where the code is

- `internal/manifest`: tree construction (`treebuild.go`), writing and settings (`submanifest_write.go`), reading (`tree.go`).
- `internal/sync/submanifest.go`: the capability gate, both pragmas, and configuration exchange of the settings.
- `repo_submanifest.go` and `cli/repo_submanifests.go`: the public API and command.

---

# Sparse cones

URL: https://libfossil-docs.daniel-mestas.workers.dev/docs/concepts/sparse-cones/


A repository does not have to hold everything. A **cone** limits it by path. A [horizon](/docs/concepts/horizons/) limits it by age, and is carried as a member of a cone. Both leave the history intact, and the blobs they skip can be fetched later.

Cones follow `draft-fossil-sparse-cone-00`. They are implemented in step with zit.

## Cones

A cone is a set of repository paths. Each member is a directory subtree or a single file, and each is either an include or an exclude. Members are literal prefixes, not patterns (§3.4).

The longest member that covers a path decides it. An exclude carves a part out of an include, and a deeper include re-includes part of an exclude (§3.3):

```
include src
exclude src/vendor
include src/vendor/keep
```

`src/a.c` is covered. `src/vendor/v.c` is not. `src/vendor/keep/k.c` is covered again.

A cone must have at least one include, at most 255 members, and no exclude that no include covers. Order does not matter; members are sorted and reduced to the smallest set with the same coverage (§3.2).

### Checkout cones and store cones

A **checkout cone** limits the working directory (§4). The repository still holds every file. A sparse checkout writes, scans and tracks only the covered files. A commit carries the uncovered files from its parent unchanged, so it is the same check-in a dense checkout would make. Adding, removing, renaming or reverting an uncovered path fails with `ErrOutsideCone`.

A **store cone** limits the repository itself (§5). Blobs outside the cone are not fetched, and can be dropped by compaction. A checkout opens over a sparse store only if its own cone stays inside the store's.

Manifests, [sub-manifest](/docs/concepts/sub-manifests/) nodes and control artifacts are always held, so the whole history stays readable. Only file content is elided.

### Elided is not damaged

An artifact the store lacks is classified one of three ways (§5.2):

- **transit**: not here yet, and sync will ask for it.
- **shunned**: deliberately refused.
- **elided**: the cone says the store need not hold it.

Only elided is by design. Sync never requests an elided artifact, whether the store is the client or the server, and `verify` reports a store that is complete within its cone as OK. Elision is computed from the cone and never stored, so changing the cone reclassifies. Losing the cone, or one this version cannot read, turns every elided artifact back into a transit one and the store heals toward dense.

## Library usage

### Build a cone

```go
cone, err := libfossil.NewCone(
    []string{"src", "docs"},       // include
    []string{"src/vendor"},        // exclude
)
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}
fmt.Println(cone.Covers("src/main.go"))           // true
covered, member := cone.Decide("src/vendor/x.c")  // false, "src/vendor"
```

A `Cone` is immutable. `With`, `Without` and `WithHorizon` return new ones. `Include`, `Exclude`, `Digest`, `String` and `Horizon` read it.

### Sparse checkout

```go
repo, err := libfossil.Open("repo.fossil")
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}
defer repo.Close()

co, err := repo.CreateCheckout("work", libfossil.CheckoutCreateOpts{Cone: cone})
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}
defer co.Close()

// Widen, narrow, or pass nil to make the checkout dense.
change, err := co.SetCone(wider)
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}
fmt.Println(change.Materialized, change.Dematerialized)
```

`SetCone` writes the files the new cone adds and removes the ones it drops from the working directory. The repository keeps them. It refuses, changing nothing, when a file leaving the cone has local changes or a file entering it would overwrite an untracked one. A cone that carries a horizon fails with `ErrHorizonCheckout`.

Over a sparse store, widening needs content the store may not hold. `SetConeContext` takes a `RequiredContentOpts{Peer: transport}` and fetches it. With no peer the widening is refused and nothing changes.

### Clone into a sparse store

```go
t := libfossil.NewHTTPTransport("https://example.com/repo")
repo, res, err := libfossil.Clone(ctx, "repo.fossil", t, libfossil.CloneOpts{
    StoreCone: cone,
})
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}
defer repo.Close()
fmt.Println(res.Elided, res.ConeServed)
```

The result counts:

- `Elided`: artifacts left absent under the cone.
- `ConeServed`: replies where the server acknowledged applying the cone (`pragma cone-served`, §6.3). The other rounds were served densely and filtered locally.

Both are zero for a dense clone. `SyncResult` has the same fields. A server that will not serve a sparse clone refuses it. A cone with a horizon clones a horizon store; see [Horizons](/docs/concepts/horizons/).

### Set, widen and drop on an existing store

```go
// Set or replace, without a peer. Narrowing deletes nothing.
err = repo.SetStoreCone(next)

// Read it.
cur, err := repo.StoreCone()

// Widen, and fetch what that newly covers.
sr, err := repo.SetStoreConeContext(ctx, wider, libfossil.RequiredContentOpts{
    Peer: t,
})

// Drop the cone. Fetch everything it elided.
sr, err = repo.SetStoreConeContext(ctx, nil, libfossil.RequiredContentOpts{Peer: t})

// Drop held blobs the cone elides. See Limits.
n, err := repo.CompactStore(ctx)
```

`SetStoreCone` moves no content. Widening makes the newly covered elided artifacts wanted again, and the next pull fetches them. `SetStoreConeContext` does the pull itself through an ordinary cone-scoped sync. With artifacts to fetch and no `Peer`, it refuses, names the count, and leaves the cone unchanged. If the transfer fails after the cone is replaced, the wider policy stays and the next pull heals it. While a store cone is set, a commit carries no R card. `CompactStore` on a dense store fails with `ErrNoStoreCone`.

## Command line

### Open a sparse checkout

```
libfossil -R repo.fossil repo open [DIR] --cone src --cone docs --cone-not src/vendor
```

- `--cone=CONE,...`: make a sparse checkout; materialize and track only this path's subtree (repeatable).
- `--cone-not=CONE-NOT,...`: exclude this path's subtree from an enclosing `--cone` (repeatable).

### Edit the checkout cone

All of these take `-d, --dir` for the checkout directory (default `.`).

```
libfossil repo cone show
libfossil repo cone add src/extra
libfossil repo cone add --not src/gen
libfossil repo cone remove src/extra
libfossil repo cone set src docs --not src/vendor
libfossil repo cone dense
libfossil repo cone test src/a.c src/vendor/v.c
```

- `show`: list the cone's members ("dense" when there is none).
- `add <paths>`: widen the cone, or with `--not` carve paths out of it.
- `remove <paths>`: remove members of either polarity.
- `set <paths>`: replace the cone. `--not` takes the exclusions.
- `dense`: drop the cone and materialize every file.
- `test <paths>`: classify paths against the cone and name the deciding member. It exits non-zero when any path is elided, so it works as a predicate. `-q` prints nothing and reports through the status only.

`add`, `remove`, `set` and `dense` can need content the store lacks. They take `--remote` (default: the saved last-sync-url), `--sync-user`, `--sync-pass` (never saved), `--sync-private` and `--timeout` (default 10m; 0 disables it).

### Clone a sparse store

```
libfossil repo clone URL repo.fossil --cone src --cone-not src/vendor
```

- `--cone=CONE,...`: clone a sparse store: fetch only this path's subtree (repeatable).
- `--cone-not=CONE-NOT,...`: carve this path out of a `--cone` (repeatable).

`--horizon`, `--leaves`, `--structural` and `--seed-key` combine with these; see [Horizons](/docs/concepts/horizons/).

### Change the store cone

```
libfossil -R repo.fossil repo cone store                          # show it
libfossil -R repo.fossil repo cone store src docs --not src/vendor
libfossil -R repo.fossil repo cone store --dense
libfossil -R repo.fossil repo cone compact
```

- With no paths, `store` shows the store cone. With paths, it replaces it and fetches what the widening covers. `--not` takes the exclusions.
- `--dense`: drop the store cone, fetching everything it elided.
- `compact`: drop held blobs the store cone elides (irreversible locally).

`store` takes the same `--remote`, `--sync-user`, `--sync-pass`, `--sync-private` and `--timeout` flags as above. Its `--horizon`, `--leaves`, `--structural` and `--no-horizon` flags are described under [Horizons](/docs/concepts/horizons/).

## Interoperability

**zit.** The cone format matches zit's byte for byte, so a cone's digest is the same in both. Sparse sync works in both directions against zit's `horizon-rfc` revision. An implementation that predates horizons refuses a cone that carries one.

**Stock fossil 2.28.** A sparse store must not be served as if it were dense, because the clone would be silently incomplete. A store held sparsely is served only when its `partial-mirror` setting is on (`repo config set partial-mirror on`, `SettingPartialMirror`); otherwise it refuses. The refusal puts the push card ahead of the error so fossil 2.28 aborts instead of carrying on. Fossil cannot read [sub-manifest](/docs/concepts/sub-manifests/) check-ins either, so a repository that uses them is for libfossil and zit peers only.

## Limits

- **Compaction is irreversible locally.** `CompactStore` and `repo cone compact` delete held blobs (§5.4). Widening later fetches them again, which needs a peer that still has them. Structural artifacts, sub-manifest nodes, unsent or private content and the delta bases of retained artifacts are kept.
- **A sparse store lacks file content.** Commands that read an elided blob need a peer to fetch it, or fail.
- **A cone is not an authorization boundary** (§6.5). It limits what a store holds and asks for, not what a peer may read.

---

# Horizons

URL: https://libfossil-docs.daniel-mestas.workers.dev/docs/concepts/horizons/


A horizon cuts a store by time. It names a check-in **C**, a rule, and a depth. The check-ins the rule keeps are the **held set**. A blob is elided when no check-in in the held set names it. Structure (manifests, tags, control artifacts) is never elided by a content horizon.

A horizon is a member of a store cone, so everything on [Sparse cones](/docs/concepts/sparse-cones/) about store cones, elided artifacts and compaction applies to it too. The behaviour follows `draft-fossil-horizon-00`, implemented in step with zit.

The held set is computed from the check-in graph the repository holds. It is stored nowhere (§3.1).

## Rules

- **descendants** (the default): C and every check-in descended from it, through any parent, merges included.
- **leaves**: the descendants, plus, for every childless check-in that does not descend from C, every descendant of each check-in where its ancestry meets C's.

A check-in is childless when no other check-in names it as a parent, open or closed. A branch tip merged into another branch has a child, so it is not childless. Under the leaves rule, any two childless check-ins have their merge base in the held set, so merging branches that are still being extended never crosses the horizon. Both rules give a set that includes every child of every check-in in it.

The leaves rule has a cost you should check before using it. An old branch that was never merged forks from C's ancestry near the root, and the rule then holds every descendant of that fork. On fossil-scm.org's repository it held 20,907 of 21,008 check-ins at every depth tried. The descendants rule, with C 10, 100, 426 and 1000 check-ins back from the tip, saves 97, 86, 56 and 41 percent of that history (§3.4). Use the leaves rule when the repository keeps few old unmerged branches.

`repo cone cost <check-in>` (`Repo.HorizonCost`) reports what each rule would hold at a check-in, read from a repository that has the history:

```
$ libfossil -R repo.fossil repo cone cost trunk
horizon at trunk
descendants  1 check-ins, 3 blobs, 6 B expanded, 57 B stored
leaves  1 check-ins, 3 blobs, 6 B expanded, 57 B stored
```

## Depth

- **content** (the default): which blobs are held. Every check-in's structure is still held (§4).
- **structural** (`Horizon.Structural`, `--structural`): also cuts the manifests below C (§5). It needs a seed, a control artifact the origin mints so a clone can derive tag and branch state without C's ancestry.

A content horizon keeps all structure and elides only blobs; a structural horizon also leaves out the manifests below C.

## Seeds are never pushed

A seed is private to the clone that holds it, so a go-libfossil origin refuses any pushed control artifact that looks like one (§5.2.3 and its F.1 erratum):

- its U card is `go-libfossil`, the label go-libfossil writes on every seed it mints; or
- it carries a `horizon-seed` T card, whatever its U card.

The test runs when the artifact first becomes readable, on its content after any delta is applied. A push that carries a seed the origin can read within that push is refused whole: nothing it carried is stored, and the reply is one error card, `seed refused: a seed is private to the clone that holds it; it is never pushed`, which a go-libfossil pusher reports among its sync errors. A delta whose base has not arrived is stored as any dangling delta is, and withheld, never announced or sent, until something supplies the base: a later push, a pull, or a check-in or tag that writes the same bytes. That supplies only the base, so it is stored as usual, with no error, and the seed is refused then.

A refused seed's hash is recorded in a table of the store's own that no configuration group carries, so no peer pulls it. The seed stays stored, so a delta built on it stays readable, but it is never linked, announced or sent, and a re-push of it is refused at once. Pulling the same hash from a peer stores nothing new: the row is already held, and stays refused. Any other seed-shaped artifact a store receives by pull or clone is an ordinary control artifact.

Two consequences follow:

- Another implementation's label alone is ordinary. A control artifact under zit's `U zit-seed` with no `horizon-seed` T card is stored when pushed; one that carries a `horizon-seed` card is refused.
- A user whose login is `go-libfossil` cannot push control artifacts (tags, branch moves, closes) to a go-libfossil origin, since they carry that login as their U card. go-libfossil does not forbid the login; do not give it to a user.

## The binding card

Every seed names the horizon it was minted for in one card (§5.2.1):

```
T +horizon-seed <C> <rule>
```

The card is part of the seed's bytes, so a signature covers it. It is not a tag in force: a clone skips it when it applies the seed, and an origin never derives a `horizon-seed` tag it holds into a seed. It does not count as the one T card a control artifact needs, so with no other tag in force there is still no seed.

Before it holds a seed, signed or not, a clone checks it (§5.2.4):

- it carries exactly one binding card, and that card names the clone's own C and rule;
- its D card is not earlier than that of the seed the clone already holds. A newer tag state never gives an earlier D, so an earlier one is a replay. An equal D is accepted.

A seed that fails either check is refused as a wrongly signed one: the clone falls back to the content horizon, completes, and reports `HorizonFallback`; later pulls keep the content horizon. A deepen discards the held seed first, so the floor starts again at the new C. A held seed that is no longer bound to the store's horizon is discarded when it is next applied, as one that fails its signature is. A seed held by v0.15.0, which carried no binding card, is replaced on the first pull from an origin that binds its seeds; a rebuild before that discards it, and the next pull fetches a bound one.

zit 0.7.1 writes and checks the same card, so the two implementations' seeds for one repository are byte-identical up to the U card.

## Signed seeds

An origin signs each seed it mints with its `horizon-seed-command`, configured apart from the `clearsign` and `pgp-command` settings that sign check-ins (§5.2.4). An origin with no seed command sends its seeds unsigned, even when it signs check-ins. It keeps one signature per seed, so a seed keeps its name while the tag state it records is unchanged.

A clone given the origin's public key verifies every seed against it: at clone time, on every pull, and when it rebuilds. A seed that is unsigned, or signed by another key, is discarded and the clone falls back to the content horizon. A clone with no key accepts an unsigned seed. The key is the clone's own `horizon-seed-key` setting, never something the origin sends. `CloneOpts.SeedKey` and `repo clone --seed-key` set it when the clone is made; `Repo.SetConfig` refuses a value that is neither an SSH public key nor an OpenPGP fingerprint.

- **SSH:** the origin signs with `ssh-keygen -q -Y sign -n fossil-horizon-seed -f KEY`; the clone's key is the public key line, verified in process. The namespace is `fossil-horizon-seed`, never the check-in namespace `fossilscm`, so a signature on a check-in or tag cannot stand in for a seed's. An origin whose seed command signs in another namespace serves no seed: the request fails.
- **PGP:** the origin signs with a `gpg --clearsign -o` command; the clone's key is the key's 40 or 64 digit fingerprint, verified by `gpg` against the user's keyring. PGP has no namespace and relies on the binding card alone.

```
libfossil -R repo.fossil repo config set horizon-seed-command \
    "ssh-keygen -q -Y sign -n fossil-horizon-seed -f ~/.ssh/id_ed25519"
```

An origin signs only for a requester that may read, after the request is authorized, and keeps the signature in its own table; a store that cannot write, such as a read-only mirror, signs again for every request. Setting the origin's own `horizon-seed-key` to its public key makes it check a kept signature before serving it, so replacing the key behind an unchanged seed command takes effect at once. A clone that cannot run its verifier (gpg missing, or timed out) keeps the seed it holds and reports the error rather than falling back. Settings are read from the repository only: go-libfossil reads no global fossil configuration.

[Signing](/docs/concepts/signing/) covers the signing settings and the verifier in more detail.

## Moving the horizon

Moving C earlier and pulling fetches what the deeper horizon keeps. Moving it later keeps what you hold until you compact. A horizon store cannot be a checkout's cone: a horizon governs what the repository holds, not which paths a checkout writes.

## Library usage

### Build a horizon cone

```go
h := libfossil.Horizon{
    Checkin:    "9f2c...",                   // full 40 or 64 digit hash
    Rule:       libfossil.HorizonDescendants, // or HorizonLeaves
    Structural: false,                        // true for the structural cut
}

// Horizon only: every path, cut by time.
hc, err := libfossil.NewHorizonCone(nil, nil, h)

// Horizon plus paths.
hc, err = libfossil.NewHorizonCone([]string{"src"}, nil, h)

got, ok := hc.Horizon()               // read it back
noHorizon, err := hc.WithHorizon(nil) // drop it, keep the paths
```

`Checkin` must be a full hash, and it is lower-cased. Dropping the horizon of a horizon-only cone is an error, since nothing would be left; use `SetStoreCone(nil)` to make the store dense.

### Clone into a horizon store

```go
t := libfossil.NewHTTPTransport("https://example.com/repo")
repo, res, err := libfossil.Clone(ctx, "repo.fossil", t, libfossil.CloneOpts{
    StoreCone: hc,
    SeedKey:   "ssh-ed25519 AAAA...", // optional; structural only
})
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}
defer repo.Close()
fmt.Println(res.Elided, res.HorizonServed, res.StructuralServed, res.HorizonFallback)
```

- `HorizonServed`: replies where the server cut at the horizon (`pragma horizon-served`, §6.2.5). The other rounds were classified locally.
- `StructuralServed`: those served at the structural level.
- `HorizonFallback`: a structural clone kept the content horizon instead (§6.3).

`SyncResult` has the same fields.

### Clone by name or depth

A clone has no history yet, so it cannot turn a branch name or a count into C. It asks the origin, which resolves the name once, in its first reply (§6.2.7):

```go
repo, res, err := libfossil.Clone(ctx, "repo.fossil", t, libfossil.CloneOpts{
    Horizon: &libfossil.Horizon{
        Checkin: "trunk",                 // "tip", a branch or tag, or a full hash
        Rule:    libfossil.HorizonLeaves, // and Structural, as for any horizon
    },
    HorizonDepth: 100, // step back 100 check-ins along primary parents
})
fmt.Println(res.HorizonResolved, res.HorizonSteps, res.HorizonResolvedLocally)
```

- `tip` is the most recent check-in. A full hash names that check-in. Any other name is the most recent check-in carrying the tag `sym-NAME`, so branches and tags both work. Two check-ins with the same time resolve to the one with the lower full hash, so every origin resolves a name alike. Hash prefixes are not resolved.
- `HorizonDepth` steps back along primary parents. If history runs out first, C is the root it stopped at and `HorizonSteps` is less than the depth asked for.
- The store records only the resolved hash. Every later request of the clone, and every later pull, sync or deepen, sends that hash, never the name.
- A name the origin cannot resolve fails the clone with `horizon name not found: NAME`, and nothing is left on disk.

`CloneOpts.Horizon` takes the same `Horizon` as a store cone, except that its `Checkin` may be a name. `StoreCone` then gives only the path members: giving a horizon on both is an error, as is `HorizonDepth` without `Horizon`. A full hash is sent as a name too: the origin tries it as a check-in hash first and then as a branch or tag, so a branch spelled as 40 hex digits is found. A structural clone by name gets the seed the origin mints for the resolved C.

An origin resolves a name only for a requester that may read or clone. To anyone else it answers as if the request named no horizon, so whether a name exists cannot be learned from its replies.

An origin that does not answer the name (stock fossil, zit 0.7.0 and earlier) serves the clone densely. The clone then resolves the name itself over what it received, classifies locally at the content horizon, and reports `HorizonResolvedLocally`; a structural request falls back to the content horizon and reports `HorizonFallback` (§6.3).

`HorizonHistoryURL`, on both results, is the address the origin gives for querying history below the horizon outside the sync protocol, when it gives one. An origin sets it with `repo config set horizon-history-url https://...` (`SettingHorizonHistoryURL`); only one http or https URL with no spaces or credentials is accepted. `repo clone` prints it as `History:`.

### Deepen, merge across, and verify the seed

Setting, replacing and dropping a horizon on an existing store use `SetStoreCone` and `SetStoreConeContext`, as for any [store cone](/docs/concepts/sparse-cones/).

```go
// Move the horizon down far enough to reach a check-in, which may lie
// below it. C moves to that check-in when it is an ancestor of C, else to
// a common ancestor of the two, asked of the origin when the store cannot
// see one. The rule, the depth and the path members stay.
sr, err := repo.DeepenHorizon(ctx, target, libfossil.RequiredContentOpts{Peer: t})

// Merge. With a Peer, a merge where either side's ancestry crosses a
// structural horizon asks the origin for the base, deepening to it when it
// lies below. Without one it fails with an error matching
// libfossil.ErrBelowHorizon, even when the store finds a base it holds.
mr, err := co.MergeContext(ctx, libfossil.CheckoutMergeOpts{Version: rid},
    libfossil.RequiredContentOpts{Peer: t})

// Check the seed against the history it summarizes. This fetches every
// manifest below C and leaves a content-horizon store.
v, err := repo.VerifySeed(ctx, libfossil.RequiredContentOpts{Peer: t})
```

Deepening a structural store discards its seed before it fetches the new one, so the old seed cannot shadow the new one. If the transfer fails, the old horizon and seed are put back (§5.8).

A merge never runs against a base the store does not hold. A bisection whose good end lies below the horizon is refused the same way, naming the horizon and the deepen.

An origin checks each pushed check-in that creates a branch: if the branch it cancels is not the one this origin derives for the parent, the clone's seed was stale, and the whole push is refused with `stale seed: ...` (§5.7). Pull, push a control artifact that cancels the parent's real branch tag on the check-in, and push again.

## Command line

### Clone a horizon store

```
libfossil repo clone URL repo.fossil --horizon <full hash>
libfossil repo clone URL repo.fossil --horizon trunk --depth 100
libfossil repo clone URL repo.fossil --horizon tip --leaves --cone src
libfossil repo clone URL repo.fossil --horizon release --structural --seed-key "ssh-ed25519 AAAA..."
```

- `--horizon=STRING`: clone a horizon store: elide blobs below this check-in, given as `tip`, a branch or tag, or its full 40 or 64 digit hash.
- `--depth=N`: with `--horizon`, step the check-in back N check-ins along primary parents, stopping at a root.
- `--leaves`: with `--horizon`, also hold every open leaf's ancestry back to the check-in.
- `--structural`: with `--horizon`, also elide the manifests below the check-in, deriving their branch and tag state from the origin's seed.
- `--seed-key=STRING`: the origin's public key, an SSH public key line or an OpenPGP fingerprint. With `--structural`, a seed not signed by it is discarded and the clone falls back to the content horizon. It is kept as the `horizon-seed-key` setting.

`--cone` and `--cone-not` combine with these. The origin resolves a name, since nothing is local yet to resolve it against, and the clone prints the check-in it resolved to as `Horizon at:`. A full hash is sent as a name too, so the origin can also find a branch or tag spelled as one. Later pulls, syncs and deepens send the resolved hash.

### Change the horizon

```
libfossil -R repo.fossil repo cone store --horizon <check-in>
libfossil -R repo.fossil repo cone store --horizon <check-in> --leaves
libfossil -R repo.fossil repo cone store --horizon <check-in> --structural
libfossil -R repo.fossil repo cone store --no-horizon
libfossil -R repo.fossil repo cone deepen <check-in>
libfossil -R repo.fossil repo cone cost <check-in>
```

- `--horizon=STRING`: elide blobs below this check-in (name, branch or hash prefix), fetching what a deeper horizon keeps. Unlike `clone`, a local name is fine.
- `--leaves`: with `--horizon`, also hold every open leaf's ancestry back to the check-in.
- `--structural`: with `--horizon`, also elide the manifests below the check-in; the next pull fetches the origin's seed.
- `--no-horizon`: drop the horizon, keeping the path members, and fetch what it elided.
- `cone deepen`: move the horizon down to reach the check-in, fetching what the deeper horizon keeps.
- `cone cost`: report what each rule would hold at the check-in, from this repository.

### Merge and verify

```
libfossil -R repo.fossil repo merge <version> -d DIR
libfossil -R repo.fossil repo verify --seed
```

- `merge`: a merge where either side's ancestry crosses a structural horizon asks the remote for the base, and deepens to it when it lies below. A merge whose ancestry stays above the horizon contacts no peer.
- `verify --seed`: verify the structural seed by fetching the history below the horizon. The store stays a content-horizon store.

`store`, `deepen`, `merge` and `verify` take `--remote` (default: the saved last-sync-url), `--sync-user`, `--sync-pass` (never saved), `--sync-private` and `--timeout` (default 10m; 0 disables it).

## Interoperability

**zit.** The horizon format matches zit's byte for byte. Horizon sync works in both directions against zit's `horizon-rfc` revision.

**Stock fossil 2.28.** A horizon store refuses a dense clone, because the clone would be silently incomplete.

**zit 0.7.1** resolves horizon names and depths as go-libfossil's origin does. Against zit 0.7.0 and earlier a clone by name falls back to resolving locally.

**A peer that knows nothing of horizons.** A horizon clone from stock Fossil works, by hash or by name. The client asks for nothing below the horizon, records the below-horizon blobs it is sent as elided instead of storing them, and classifies locally. `HorizonServed` stays 0. Stock Fossil can announce a new check-in only inside a cluster. A horizon store holds no clusters, so it requests the cluster members as transit and classifies what arrives (§4.5). Without that a new check-in would not be learned until a later one named it.

## Limits

- **The structural horizon needs an origin that serves it.** Against a peer that does not answer `horizon-served structural` (stock fossil, or a server without a current seed) the clone falls back to the content horizon and reports `HorizonFallback` (§6.3).
- **PGP verification needs gpg.** A PGP-signed seed is verified by running `gpg`, so a clone keyed with a fingerprint needs gpg installed and the key in its keyring; on js/wasm only SSH keys verify. gpg-agent hangs at start under a very large open-file limit, which a macOS shell can set to 2^31 (`ulimit -n`): lower it, to 4096 say, in the environment that signs or verifies with gpg.
- **The horizon cursor needs a transport that names its peer.** The cursor (`pragma horizon-cursor`, §6.2.6) lets an exchange skip re-announcing what both sides hold. The HTTP transport keys it by URL; a custom `Transport` keeps none and announces in full.
- **A horizon is not a checkout cone.** Give a checkout a horizon and you get `ErrHorizonCheckout`.
- **Compaction is irreversible locally.** `repo cone compact` drops the held blobs below the horizon; deepening later needs a peer that still has them.

---

# Signing

URL: https://libfossil-docs.daniel-mestas.workers.dev/docs/concepts/signing/


go-libfossil signs two kinds of artifact: check-ins, as fossil and zit sign them, and the seeds an origin mints for [structural horizons](/docs/concepts/horizons/). Each has its own signing command, and both use the same two envelopes, a PGP clear-signed message or the SSH envelope fossil builds around a detached `ssh-keygen` signature (`draft-fossil-artifact-format-00` §4.1.1).

## Settings

| Setting | Constant | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `clearsign` | `SettingClearsign` | Sign check-ins. Off by default. |
| `omitsign` | | Fossil's legacy setting. On, it turns check-in signing off again. |
| `pgp-command` | `SettingPGPCommand` | The check-in signing command. Unset, it is fossil's default, `gpg --clearsign -o `. |
| `horizon-seed-command` | `SettingHorizonSeedCommand` | The command an origin signs its horizon seeds with. Unset, seeds go out unsigned. |
| `horizon-seed-key` | `SettingHorizonSeedKey` | The public key a clone verifies its origin's seeds with. |

Settings are read from the repository only. go-libfossil reads no global fossil configuration, so values set with `fossil settings --global` do not apply.

## Signing check-ins

With `clearsign` on, every check-in a commit or a branch creation stores is signed. The command runs as fossil runs it:

- **PGP:** `COMMAND OUTFILE INFILE`, which writes a clear-signed copy of the manifest.
- **SSH:** a command whose name starts with `ssh` runs as `COMMAND INFILE` and writes a detached `INFILE.sig`, which is wrapped in fossil's SSH envelope. The namespace must be `fossilscm`.

```
libfossil -R repo.fossil repo config set clearsign on
libfossil -R repo.fossil repo config set pgp-command \
    "ssh-keygen -q -Y sign -n fossilscm -f ~/.ssh/id_ed25519"
```

The command runs through the shell, so `~` and environment variables expand. A signed check-in looks like this:

```
-----BEGIN SSH SIGNED MESSAGE-----

C signed
D 2026-10-23T20:45:21.089
F docs/x.md a09fd4d0...
...
Z 0e57ef44fd0eec16824d0a54ab247953
-----BEGIN SSH SIGNATURE-----
...
-----END SSH SIGNATURE-----
```

The stored bytes are the whole envelope, so the check-in's name is the hash of the signed bytes (§3.1). Readers strip the envelope before parsing, and the `Z` card covers the manifest inside it (§6.2).

To store one check-in unsigned, as fossil's `--nosign` does:

- `libfossil repo ci --nosign` and `libfossil repo branch new --nosign`.
- `CommitOpts.NoSign` (`Repo.Commit`) and `CheckoutCommitOpts.NoSign` (`Checkout.Checkin`).

### What fails

- **The signer fails or times out** (after two minutes). The commit is abandoned and nothing is stored.
- **The signer changes what it signs.** The envelope must strip back to exactly the manifest that was given, as zit checks it. A dash-escaped or rewritten manifest is refused rather than stored under a name its cards do not match.
- **On js/wasm** no external command can run, so signing fails there.

go-libfossil does not verify check-in signatures when it reads them. To check one, take the output of `libfossil repo cat` and run the signer's own verifier: `gpg --verify` on a PGP envelope, or, for SSH, `ssh-keygen -Y verify -n fossilscm -s SIG` with the manifest between the header and the signature block on standard input. The conformance test `TestSignedCheckin` checks that fossil and zit read the signed check-ins, and that a check-in zit signs with the same SSH key verifies here.

## Signing horizon seeds

An origin signs each structural horizon seed it mints with its `horizon-seed-command` (`draft-fossil-horizon-00` §5.2.4). The command is configured apart from check-in signing: `clearsign` and `pgp-command` never sign a seed, and an origin with no seed command sends its seeds unsigned even when it signs check-ins. It follows `pgp-command`'s contract. An SSH signer signs in the namespace `fossil-horizon-seed`, never `fossilscm`, so that a signature on a check-in or tag cannot stand in for a seed's; an origin whose seed command signs in another namespace serves no seed, and the request fails. PGP has no namespace and relies on the seed's [binding card](/docs/concepts/horizons/#the-binding-card) alone.

```
libfossil -R repo.fossil repo config set horizon-seed-command \
    "ssh-keygen -q -Y sign -n fossil-horizon-seed -f ~/.ssh/id_ed25519"
```

The origin keeps one signature per seed in its own table, so a seed keeps its name while the tag state it records is unchanged. It signs only for a requester allowed to read, after the request is authorized. A store that cannot write, such as a read-only mirror, signs again for every request.

A clone verifies seeds against its `horizon-seed-key` setting:

```go
repo, res, err := libfossil.Clone(ctx, "repo.fossil", t, libfossil.CloneOpts{
    StoreCone: hc, // a cone with a structural horizon
    SeedKey:   "ssh-ed25519 AAAA... origin",
})
```

```
libfossil repo clone URL repo.fossil --horizon <full hash> --structural \
    --seed-key "ssh-ed25519 AAAA... origin"
```

The key is an SSH public key line, verified in process, or a 40 or 64 digit OpenPGP fingerprint, verified by `gpg` against the user's keyring. `Repo.SetConfig` refuses a `horizon-seed-key` that is neither. The key is the clone's own; the origin never sends it.

The clone verifies every seed it holds: at clone time, on every pull, and when it rebuilds.

| Seed | Key set | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Signed by the key, in namespace `fossil-horizon-seed` for SSH | yes | Held. |
| Unsigned, signed by another key, or SSH-signed in another namespace | yes | Discarded; the store falls back to the content horizon. |
| Any | no | Held. A clone with no key accepts an unsigned seed. |
| Verifier could not run (gpg missing or timed out) | yes | The seed already held is kept and the error is reported. A new seed is refused. Nothing falls back. |

Whatever its signature, a seed is also refused when its binding card does not name the clone's own horizon or it is dated before the seed the clone holds; see [the binding card](/docs/concepts/horizons/#the-binding-card).

Setting the origin's own `horizon-seed-key` to its public key makes it check a kept signature before serving it, so replacing the key behind an unchanged seed command takes effect at once.

A signature proves where a seed came from, not that its derivation is right (§5.2.4). `repo verify --seed` (`Repo.VerifySeed`) checks the seed against the history it summarizes.

## Limits

- **PGP verification needs gpg** installed, with the origin's key in the keyring. On js/wasm only SSH keys verify.
- **gpg-agent hangs under a very large open-file limit.** A macOS shell can set `ulimit -n` to 2^31. Lower it, to 4096 say, in the environment that signs or verifies with gpg.

## Where the code is

- `signing.go`: the setting constants.
- `internal/clearsign`: running the signer, the SSH envelope, SSH verification in process, gpg verification.
- `internal/manifest/manifest.go`: signing a check-in before it is stored.
- `internal/sync/horizon_seedsign.go` and `internal/horizon/seed`: signing seeds at the origin and verifying them at the clone.
